label: Does the existential giver produce the particular effect through or with the secondary agent?
summary: See docs/notes/actuality-esse-research.md §11. Aquinas's De potentia q.3 a.7 and SCG III.66–70 defend application through the lower agent on the basis of being as proper effect and efficacy derived in this production. Molina, Concordia II, disp. 26 §§2–16, defends immediate cooperation in a numerically single operation and its effect. Both offer positive accounts of the same heating. Mere conservation also has a positive rival account in exercised intrinsic powers of sustained agents. An actively maintained angle and a setting maintained by a latch discriminate which agent is now responsible for the outgoing ray's location. A change of sustainer at a seam distinguishes the time of preservation from onset. The origination of one particular oscillation gives de re credit for the string starting to vibrate where the two descriptions identify the whole change. It gives no automatic credit for a contrast in pitch. The argument applies to a distinct dependent effect only with an identified efficient terminus. Nonsubsistent determinations leave the question at the patient. Actual contribution to a common operation gives local productive credit without requiring the giver to have acted on the secondary as agent.
blocker: Universality for bearers' esse does not identify the same giver's efficient contribution to every actual respect from onset, still less a directional contribution to each secondary's exercise. The proper-effect argument also requires that the powers be ordered to the giver in their operation. Shared production under Molina's account already grants the disputed effect-side contribution. Neither agreement nor a finite interpretation settles the issue against the conservationist.
